name: Descript
tagline: Text-based audio and video editor with transcription and AI tools

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Hobbyist is listed at $24/month monthly and $16/month annually.

verdictSummary: You can build transcript-based cutting for simple clips, but Descript's editor, media pipeline, AI voice/video tooling, publishing, and collaboration are a serious product.
coreLoopDIY: Transcribe media, map words to timestamps, allow text deletion to cut audio/video, then render via ffmpeg.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to avoid building and babysitting a media editor, not just for transcription.

priorArt.name: Kdenlive
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source video editor; useful alternative but not text-first SaaS clone.

notes: Great boundary case where a toy clone is easy but the product depth is obvious.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Descript (Text-based audio and video editor with transcription and AI tools). Requirements:

- Core loop: Transcribe media, map words to timestamps, allow text deletion to cut audio/video, then render via ffmpeg.
- Needs: ffmpeg.
- Needs: speech-to-text/alignment.
- Needs: desktop or web editor.
- Needs: video rendering pipeline.
- Needs: optional hosted storage.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: polished nonlinear editor; overdub/voice tools; filler-word workflows.
